description: A single rendered table (no plot panels), presented as an image with four columns and a header row: "Material state", "YS (MPa)", "UTS (MPa)" and "UE (%)", separated from the data by two horizontal rules. The four data rows read exactly: "2Al, 1 h/450 °C" with YS = 420 MPa, UTS = 935 MPa, UE = 75 %; "2Al, 650 °C/72 h" with YS = 400 MPa, UTS = 850 MPa, UE = 35 %; "8Al, 1 h/450 °C" with YS = 540 MPa, UTS = 895 MPa, UE = 65 %; and "8Al, 1 h/600 °C/24 h" with YS = 990 MPa, UTS = 1180 MPa, UE = 37 %. The caption identifies 2Al as Fe–30.5Mn–2.1Al–1.2C (wt.%) and 8Al as Fe–30.5Mn–8.0Al–1.2C (wt.%), with YS = yield strength, UTS = ultimate tensile strength and UE = uniform elongation. The table supports the citing text: within the 2Al steel the two annealing states have nearly identical yield strength (420 vs 400 MPa) and the long anneal mainly cuts uniform elongation (75 % → 35 %), whereas in the 8Al steel the long anneal (600 °C/24 h) raises yield strength from 540 to 990 MPa and UTS from 895 to 1180 MPa while UE falls from 65 % to 37 %.

observations.observation: The table lists four material states: '2Al, 1 h/450 °C', '2Al, 650 °C/72 h', '8Al, 1 h/450 °C' and '8Al, 1 h/600 °C/24 h'.
For '2Al, 1 h/450 °C' the table gives YS = 420 MPa, UTS = 935 MPa and UE = 75 %.
For '2Al, 650 °C/72 h' the table gives YS = 400 MPa, UTS = 850 MPa and UE = 35 %.
For '8Al, 1 h/450 °C' the table gives YS = 540 MPa, UTS = 895 MPa and UE = 65 %.
For '8Al, 1 h/600 °C/24 h' the table gives YS = 990 MPa, UTS = 1180 MPa and UE = 37 %.
Within the 2Al steel the two annealing states have nearly equal yield strength (420 vs 400 MPa) while UE drops from 75 % to 35 %, so the long anneal mainly reduces uniform elongation.
For the 8Al steel the long anneal (600 °C/24 h) raises YS from 540 to 990 MPa and UTS from 895 to 1180 MPa while UE decreases from 65 % to 37 %.
Across all four rows, UTS exceeds YS and UE ranges from 35 % to 75 %; the highest strength row ('8Al, 1 h/600 °C/24 h') has the second-lowest elongation.
The caption states 2Al is Fe–30.5Mn–2.1Al–1.2C (wt.%) and 8Al is Fe–30.5Mn–8.0Al–1.2C (wt.%), with YS = yield strength, UTS = ultimate tensile strength and UE = uniform elongation.
The citing text states the values of YS, UTS and UE shown in Table 1 correspond to the engineering stress-strain curves of Figure 1.
